newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Treasurer says fully supports $2.9 bln deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Treasurer says fully supports $2.9 bln deal.

text.p: New Jersey Treasurer Brian Clymer still fully supports a proposed $2.9 billion taxable pension obligation bond deal, despite a report published Thursday detailing an alternate plan, a spokeswoman said.
"We are 100 percent doing this," Mary Lou Murphy, a spokeswoman for the Treasurer, said in a telephone interview.
The Bergen Record reported on Thursday that Clymer had aired a "new pension fund plan" during an interview with the newspaper's editors and reporters.

The report said Clymer told the newspaper that the state Legislature will allow the adminstration to avoid making about $647 million of payments into the pension system even if it does not approve the $2.9 billion pension bond deal. Skipping the payments is one of the key reasons the administration proposed the bond deal in the first place.
But Murphy said the comments were about "a hypothetical" budget scenario and not meant to imply the Treasurer is devising alternatives in the event the Legislature rejects the bonds.

Lawmakers, including some Republican allies of Gov. Christine Whitman, has said they believe the bond sale is too large and fiscally irresponsible. Merrill Lynch & Co Inc is the senior manager on the proposed deal.
